How much paint do I need for a room?

By the Metre team · Updated 26 Oct 2026 · 3 min read

Short answer

Paint = (room perimeter × wall height − doors and windows) × coats ÷ coverage. Example: a 4.2 m × 3.6 m room with 2.5 m walls has 15.6 m perimeter, 39 m² of wall, about 36 m² after a door and a window, 72 m² for two coats, which is about 7.2 L at 10 m² per litre. Always check the coverage printed on the tin.

What you need

  • Room length, width and wall height
  • The size of each door and window
  • The coverage on the tin (m² per litre, or sq ft per gallon) and the number of coats

Step by step

  1. Find the wall area

    Add the room's length and width, double it for the perimeter, and multiply by the wall height.

  2. Subtract the openings

    Take away doors and windows. A door is roughly 1.6 to 2 m² (17 to 21 sq ft), and a medium window 1.2 to 1.5 m² (13 to 16 sq ft). Measure yours for a better number.

  3. Multiply by the number of coats

    Two coats is typical for a colour change. One coat can do for the same colour over a sound surface.

  4. Divide by the coverage

    Typical emulsion covers about 10 m² per litre per coat (about 350 to 400 sq ft per US gallon). The tin gives the real figure.

  5. Add the ceiling and a little extra

    Work out the ceiling as length × width and add it if you are painting it. Round up to the next tin size and keep a little for touch-ups.

Worked example (US units)

A 14 ft × 12 ft room with 8 ft walls: perimeter 52 ft, wall area 416 sq ft. Minus one door (about 21 sq ft) and two windows (about 30 sq ft) leaves about 365 sq ft. Two coats is about 730 sq ft. At 350 to 400 sq ft per gallon that is 1.8 to 2.1 gallons, so buy 2 gallons and check whether you want a touch-up quart.

Prime or not?

New plaster, stains and strong colour changes usually need a primer or an extra coat. Check the tin for the coverage on your surface, which may be lower on rough or absorbent walls.

Do it with Metre

Paint, flooring and wallpaper Pro

  1. Add the room in Home survey by tapping its floor corners and measure the wall height with the Height tool.
  2. Open the paint calculator, which subtracts doors and windows from the wall area.
  3. Enter the coats and the coverage from the tin to get the quantity.

How accurate is this?

Paint quantities are estimates. Surface, colour, application method and the coverage on the tin all change how much you use, so round up and keep the tin for touch-ups.

Measurements made with a phone are estimates. Before you cut, order or build, confirm critical dimensions with a physical tape.

Questions people ask

How do I calculate paint for a room?

Perimeter × height gives the wall area. Subtract doors and windows, multiply by the number of coats, and divide by the coverage on the tin.

How many square metres does a litre of paint cover?

Often about 10 m² per coat, but products range widely. Use the figure printed on the tin.

How many coats do I need?

Two coats is typical, especially for a colour change or over a dark colour.

How much paint for a 12 ft × 12 ft room?

With 8 ft walls the perimeter is 48 ft and the wall area 384 sq ft. Minus a door (about 21 sq ft) and two windows (about 30 sq ft) that leaves about 333 sq ft; two coats is about 666 sq ft. At 350 to 400 sq ft per gallon that is 1.7 to 1.9 gallons, so buy 2 gallons.
